_doc_: Shared MQTT and mail credentials served by credentials.php to both
the controller (running on each customer's IXHUB) and the web UI.
DEPLOYMENT:
1. Copy this file, fill in the real values.
2. Rename to match the host that will serve credentials.php — for
production that's `rbrheating.com.txt`.
3. Upload to ONE LEVEL ABOVE the site root (e.g. /home/rbrheating/),
not into /home/rbrheating/rbrheating.com/. credentials.php reads
`../<HTTP_HOST>.txt` so a request to https://rbrheating.com/
credentials.php returns the contents of /home/rbrheating/
rbrheating.com.txt verbatim.
4. Make sure the file is NOT inside the document root — Apache
would otherwise serve it directly without auth.
FIELDS:
broker         — MQTT broker hostname (no scheme)
port           — websocket port for the UI
mqtt_port      — MQTT bridge port for mosquitto (default 8883); not
the websocket port. A handover may change both.
username       — shared MQTT username
password       — shared MQTT password
mail_server    — SMTP server for verification / password-reset emails
mail_login     — SMTP login (usually the same as mail_from)
mail_password  — SMTP password
mail_from      — From: header on outgoing mail
mail_port      — optional SMTP port: 465 (implicit TLS) by default,
use 587 for STARTTLS providers
HANDOVER (optional):
`handover` is the continuity channel. It may be the passphrase itself
(the short form) or an object as below.
passphrase     — the secret given to installers in a sealed envelope.
Empty disables the channel. Generate one with:
python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))'
owner_mac      — the maintainer's own system MAC. Only this system's
PWA shows the flashing banner and can cancel from the
app; without it, use the cancellation link emailed
with the notification.
notify         — where the handover notification is emailed. If empty,
the address registered for owner_mac is used; mail_from
is the last fallback.
days           — the waiting period before controllers may switch
(default 14). The waiting period is not a delay in
the controller; it is the window in which the owner
can cancel a false request.
allow_http     — testing only: accept an http:// new site.
allow_private  — testing only: allow a private/loopback address as
the new site. Never enable this in production.
Per-system fields are NOT here — the controller's MAC is read from the
host's network interface, and the UI prompts the user for it once and
caches it in localStorage.

handover._doc_: Optional. An empty passphrase leaves the channel disabled; see the HANDOVER notes above.
